body:
@burkpojken : FYI, a workaround for the glibcxx problem is to install OpenJDK 8 and export `JAVA_HOME` to point at it, e.g.:

```
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-8-openjdk-amd64/
```

Re: build-runfiles: do you see this with `bazel run` by any chance? It seems that in that case Bazel won't use the normal action execution machinery to run "build-runfiles", see:
- https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/96145511b34a2d7be834e3eb05927674e875c813/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/runtime/commands/RunCommand.java#L546
- https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/96145511b34a2d7be834e3eb05927674e875c813/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/SymlinkTreeHelper.java#L83-L84

I think it's a bug that Bazel even supports running build-runfiles in a plain mode like this. Normally (during a build) Bazel would use the proper execution mechanism that creates a Spawn object and respects `--action_env`. I think the RunCommand should use this method instead: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/96145511b34a2d7be834e3eb05927674e875c813/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/exec/SymlinkTreeHelper.java#L108
Assigning to @ulfjack who authored the relevant lines.

Hi!
I see the problem when I do bazel build, not bazel run.
It occurs when I try to use a sh_binary from another rule in ctx.action().
I manage to avoid the problem now by using the flag --nobuild_runfile_links.
One other benefit I have seen when I use the --experimental_strict_action_env (or if I do 
env PATH=<minimal needed>  LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<minimal needed> bazel build) it that the build time is almost reduced to half to what it takes when our full env PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH is set.

Regarding the GLIBCXX problem. I have already set JAVA_HOME to jdk1.8.0_131.
The bazel version I use i own compiled 0.10.1

Hmm, not sure it is the reducing the env that made the build time so much shorter, I will have to investigate that more, so ignore that for now.
Sorry
The reduced build time was likely due to caching. Bazel reuses build outputs from previous builds as much as it can.

Hi! 
From bazel 0.13 and above it is not possible to make build-runfiles use neither the LD_LIBRARY_PATH from the environment or from --action_env=LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/app/vbuild/RHEL6-x86_64/gcc/5.2.0/lib

We cannot use the later versions of bazel now in our environment :(

Preferable for us the environment variables for LD_LIBRARY_PATH and PATH should be used in all actions if --experimental_strict_action_env is not set.
Sorry about that. I'll send out a fix.

issue.title: --action_env results in confusing and inconsistent behavior

labels.name: P3
labels.description: We're not considering working on this, but happy to review a PR. (No assignee)

repository.name: bazel

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

Bazel has two forms for passing environment variables into the build via the `--action_env` command-line parameter:

- **NAME only:** the variable is passed into Bazel, getting the value from the user's environment.
- **NAME=value:** the variable is passed into Bazel with the explicitly provided value

I have stumbled into some surprising observations:

- Variables passed via `--action_env` are not set in all task environments (e.g., compiling for host.)
- Which tasks have the variable in their environment is dependent on which form is used.

Both of these appear to be bugs based on my understanding of how `--action_env` should work from the documentation.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.
Example 1:
```
$ git clone https://github.com/crorvick/bazel-hello.git
$ cd bazel-hello
$ bazel build --action_env=MY_VARIABLE=nothing_special -s //src/hello
```
Example 2:
```
$ bazel clean
$ bazel shutdown
$ MY_VARIABLE=nothing_special bazel build --action_env=MY_VARIABLE -s //src/hello
```
In both examples tasks are run without `MY_VARIABLE` set in their environments.  The tasks that do see `MY_VARIABLE` are not consistent between the examples (i.e., example 2 sees fewer)

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

1. CentOS 7.4
2. Gentoo

(reproducible on both)

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

1. CentOS 7.4: `release 0.10.0- (@non-git)`
2. Gentoo: `release 0.7.0- (@non-git)`

### If `bazel info release` returns "development version" or "(@non-git)", tell us how you built Bazel.

1. CentOS 7.4:
   1. download tarball from GitHub (`bazel-0.10.0-dist.zip`)
   2. run `compile.sh` from exploded tarball

2. Gentoo
   1. run `emerge` with `~amd64` enabled for `dev-util/bazel`
